2282.subject: Zoology
2282.text: The type of epithelial cells which line the inner surface of Fallopian tubes, bronchioles and small bronchi are known as
2282.sol:
Ciliated epithelium is a region of epithelium consisting of columnar or cuboidal cells bearing hairlike appendages called cilia, that are capable of beating rapidly. Ciliated epithelium performs the functions of moving particles of fluids over the epithelial surface. Cubical ciliated epithelium occurs in certain parts of uriniferous tubules whereas columnar ciliated epithelium occurs in fallopian tubules, nasal passages, bronchioles, small bronchi and buccopharyngeal cavity of frog. It often occurs in the vicinity of mucus secreting goblet cells.
Squamous epithelium are found in linning of alveoli in the lungs and Bowman's capsule in the kidney. Columnar epithelium are found in the lining layer of gastrointestinal tract, gall bladder, uterus etc. and cubical or cuboidal epithelium lines the salivary ducts, pancreated ducts, gastric glands, thyroid follicles, germinal epithelium of ovary, proximal part of uriniferous tubules etc.

4305.sol:

So, Assertion is true while reason is false.

7426.subject: Mathematics
7426.text: If $a = cos\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right),$ then $Re \left(a + a^{2} + a^{3} + a^{4} + a^{5}\right) =$
7426.sol:
We have,

$a = cos\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right)$

Then,

${a}^{2} = {\left\{cos\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right)\right\}}^{2}$

      $= cos\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{11}\right)$

${a}^{3} = cos\left(\dfrac{24\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{24\pi}{11}\right)$

${a}^{4} = cos\left(\dfrac{32\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{32\pi}{11}\right)$

${a}^{5} = cos\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right)$

Now, 

$= a + {a}^{2} + {a}^{3} + {a}^{4} + {a}^{5}$

$= cos\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{24\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{24\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{32\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{32\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right)$

$= \left\{cos\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{24\pi}{11}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{32\pi}{11}\right)\right\} + cos\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right) + i\left\{sin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right) + sin\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{11}\right) + sin\left(\dfrac{24\pi}{11}\right) + sin\left(\dfrac{32\pi}{11}\right) + sin\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right)\right\}$

  $= \left\{\dfrac{cos\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11} + 4 \cdot \dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right)} \times sin\left(\dfrac{5 \times 8\pi}{11}\right)\right\} + \text{Imaginary part}$

$= \dfrac{cos\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{40\pi}{11}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{8\pi}{11}\right)} + \text{Imaginary part}$        $= \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \text{Imaginary part}$   

Therefore, $\text{Re}\left(a + {a}^{2} + {a}^{3} + {a}^{4} + {a}^{5}\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

8154.subject: Mathematics
8154.text: On solving \($\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x-y+3}{2 x-2 y+5}$\), the solution obtained is \(x=2(x-y)+\log (t)+c\), find \(t\)
8154.sol:
Given differential equation,
\(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x-y+3}{2(x-y)+5}\)
Let \(\quad x-y=t \Rightarrow 1-\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x}\), so
$\begin{array}{ll}& 1-\frac{d t}{d x}=\frac{t+3}{2 t+5} \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d x}=\frac{2 t+5-t-3}{2 t+5}=\frac{t+2}{2 t+5}\\
\Rightarrow  \int\frac{2 t+5}{t+2} d t=\int d x \\
\Rightarrow  \int \lleft(2+\frac{1}{t+2}\right)d t=x+C^{\prime} \\
\Rightarrow & 2 t+\log _e|t+2|=x+C^{\prime} \\
\Rightarrow & 2(x-y)+\log|x-y+2|+C=x \\
\Rightarrow & 2(x-y)+\log(t)+C=x \quad \text{ (given) }
\end{array}$
On comparing, we get
\(\therefore \quad t=x-y+2\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

10834.text: For a binomial variate $X$ with parameters $n = 5$ and $p = \dfrac{3}{4}$. If $\alpha = \dfrac{1}{9}P ( X \ge 3 )$ and $\beta = P ( X \le 2 )$, then $256 ( \beta - \alpha ) =$
10834.sol:
We know that the binomial distribution is given by

$P\left(X = r\right) = Cr n \left({p}^{r}{q}^{n - r}\right)$ 

and $p + q = 1$.

Now, we have 

$n = 5, p = \dfrac{3}{4}, q = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Now, 

$\alpha = \dfrac{1}{9}P ( X \ge 3 )$$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{9}\left\{P ( X = 3 ) + P ( X = 4 ) + P ( X = 5 )\right\}$

$= \dfrac{1}{9}\left\{C3 5 {\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{3}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + C4 5 {\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{4}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{1} + C5 5 {\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{5}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{0}\right\}$

$= \dfrac{102}{{4}^{5}}$

And,

$\beta = P ( X \le 2 )$

14698.text: The radius of Earth is about $6400 \mathrm{ km}$ and that of Mars is $3200 \mathrm{ km}$, and mass of the Earth is about 10 times mass of Mars. An object weight $200 \mathrm{ N}$ on the surface of Earth. Then, its weight on the surface of Mars will be
14698.sol:
Given, radius of Earth and Mars are $6400 \mathrm{ km}$ and $3200 \mathrm{ km}$, respectively.
Mass of Earth $=10$ (Mass of Mars)
$M_e=10 M_m$
We know that, acceleration due to gravity at surface of a planet is
$g=\frac{G M}{R^2},$
where, $M=$ mass of planet
and $R=$ radius of planet.
Taking the ratio of acceleration due to gravity of Mars to Earth,
$\frac{g_m}{g_e}=\frac{\frac{G M_m}{R_m^2}}{\frac{G M_e}{R_e^2}}=\frac{M_m}{M_e} \times\left(\frac{R_e}{R_m}\right)^2$
By substituting the values, we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{g_m}{g_e}=\frac{1}{10} \times\left(\frac{6400}{3200}\right)^2=\frac{1}{10} \times 4 \\ & g_m=\frac{2}{5} g_e\end{aligned}$
Given, the weight on earth's surface,
$w_e=m g_e=200 \mathrm{ N}\therefore$ Weight on the Mars surface,
$w_m=m g_m=\frac{2}{5}\left(m g_e\right)=\frac{2}{5} \times 200 \mathrm{ N}=80 \mathrm{ N}$

19511.subject: Chemistry
19511.text: Choose the correct order of increasing acidic strength of the following compounds.
19511.sol:
The acidic strength of alcohols depends on the stability of the conjugate base (alkoxide ion) formed after the loss of a proton. The stability of the alkoxide ion is increased by the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) through the inductive effect (-I effect).

The compounds are $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, and $\mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$.

In $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, the ethyl group is electron-donating (+I effect), which destabilizes the alkoxide ion, making it the least acidic.

In $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, the halogen atoms exert a strong -I effect. Fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine, so the -I effect of the $\mathrm{CF}_3$ group is stronger than that of the $\mathrm{CCl}_3$ group.

Stronger -I effect leads to greater stabilization of the negative charge on the oxygen atom, resulting in higher acidic strength. Therefore, the order of increasing acidic strength is $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH} < \mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH} < \mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}<\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}<\mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$

20375.subject: Chemistry
20375.text: The decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitutions is:
20375.sol:
Reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution depends on the electron density of the benzene ring. Electron-donating groups (EDG) increase the electron density and activate the ring, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease the electron density and deactivate the ring.

Let us analyze the given compounds:
1. Compound (III) has an $-\text{OCH}_3$ group. It is a strongly activating group due to its strong $+R$ (resonance) effect, which outweighs its $-I$ effect.
2. Compound (I) has a $-\text{CH}_3$ group. It is an activating group due to its $+I$ (inductive) and $+H$ (hyperconjugation) effects. The $+R$ effect of $-\text{OCH}_3$ is stronger than the $+H$ effect of $-\text{CH}_3$, making compound (III) more reactive than compound (I).
3. Compound (II) is benzene, which has no substituents and serves as the reference.
4. Compound (IV) has a $-\text{CF}_3$ group. It is a strongly deactivating group due to its strong $-I$ effect.

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution is III > I > II > IV.

Answer: $III > I > II > IV$

20656.subject: Chemistry
20656.text: Given that the freezing point of benzene is $5.48^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and its $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}$ value is $5.12{ }^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}$. What would be the freezing point of a solution of $20 \mathrm{ g}$ of propane in $400 \mathrm{ g}$ of benzene?
20656.sol:
The molar mass of propane ($C_{3}H_{8}$) is $3 \times 12 + 8 \times 1 = 44 \text{ g/mol}$.

The number of moles of propane is $n = \dfrac{20 \text{ g}}{44 \text{ g/mol}} = \dfrac{5}{11} \text{ mol} \approx 0.4545 \text{ mol}$.

The mass of the solvent (benzene) is $400 \text{ g} = 0.4 \text{ kg}$.

The molality ($m$) of the solution is $m = \dfrac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}} = \dfrac{5/11}{0.4} = \dfrac{5}{4.4} = \dfrac{50}{44} = \dfrac{25}{22} \text{ m} \approx 1.136 \text{ m}$.

The depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_{f} = K_{f} \times m$.

Substituting the values, $\Delta T_{f} = 5.12 \times \dfrac{25}{22} = \dfrac{128}{22} \approx 5.818^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C}$.

The freezing point of the solution is $T_{f} = T_f^{{}^{\circ}} - \Delta T_{f} = 5.48^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} - 5.818^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} = -0.338^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} \approx -0.34^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C}$.

Answer: $-0.34^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$

21436.text: If the foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{25}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ and the hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{144}-\frac{y^{2}}{81}=\frac{1}{25}$ coincide, then the value of $b^{2}$ is

Eccentricity for $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ is $b^{2}=a^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right)$ and eccentricity for $\frac{x^{2}}{\frac{144}{25}}-\frac{y^{2}}{\frac{81}{25}}=1$ is
Again, foci $=a_{1} e_{1}=\frac{12}{5} \times \frac{15}{12}=3$
So, focus of hyperbola is $(3,0)=(a e, 0)$
and focus of ellipse is $(a e, 0)=(5 a, 0)$
As, this foci are same, so
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 5 a=3 \\
\therefore & e &=\frac{3}{5} \\
& \text{ So, } \quad & e^{2} &=1-\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}=1-\frac{b^{2}}{25} \\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{b^{2}}{25} &=1-e^{2}=1-\frac{9}{25} \\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{b^{2}}{25} &=\frac{16}{25} \\
\Rightarrow & & b^{2} &=16
\end{aligned}
$$

21814.subject: Mathematics
21814.text: In the parabola $y^2=4 a x$ the length of the latus rectum is 6 units and there is a chord passing through its vertex and the negative end of the latus rectum. Then the equation of the chord is
21814.sol:
The equation of the parabola is $y^2 = 4ax$. The length of the latus rectum is given as $4a = 6$, which implies $a = \dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

The coordinates of the vertex are $(0,0)$. The endpoints of the latus rectum are $(a, 2a)$ and $(a, -2a)$. The negative end of the latus rectum is $(a, -2a)$.

Substituting $a = \dfrac{3}{2}$, the coordinates of the negative end of the latus rectum are $(\dfrac{3}{2}, -2 \times \dfrac{3}{2}) = (\dfrac{3}{2}, -3)$.

The chord passes through the vertex $(0,0)$ and the point $(\dfrac{3}{2}, -3)$. The slope $m$ of this chord is $m = \dfrac{-3 - 0}{\dfrac{3}{2} - 0} = \dfrac{-3}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = -2$.

The equation of the line passing through the origin with slope $m = -2$ is $y = -2x$, which can be rewritten as $2x + y = 0$.

Answer: $2 x+y=0$

23130.text: Calculate the vapour pressure that can help the formation of a spherical droplet of water of radius $6.25 \times 10^{-5}$ m at 22°C. Given: The surface tension of water at the given temperature is $7.28 \times 10^{-2}$ Nm^{-1}$.$
23130.sol:
The excess pressure inside a spherical droplet that helps in its formation is given by the formula:

$\Delta P = \dfrac{2T}{r}$

where $T$ is the surface tension and $r$ is the radius of the droplet.

Substituting the given values:
$T = 7.28 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{N m}^{-1}$
$r = 6.25 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{m}$

$\Delta P = \dfrac{2 \times 7.28 \times 10^{-2}}{6.25 \times 10^{-5}}$

$\Delta P = \dfrac{14.56 \times 10^{-2}}{6.25 \times 10^{-5}}$

$\Delta P = 2.3296 \times 10^3\ \text{Pa}$

$\Delta P \approx 2.33 \times 10^3\ \text{Pa}$

Answer: $2.33 \times 10^3\ Pa$

23368.subject: Physics
23368.text: Figure below shows a lens of refractive index, $\mu=1.4$. $C_1$ and $C_2$ are the centres of curvature of the two faces of the lens of radii of curvature $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $8 \mathrm{ cm}$ respectively. The lens behaves as a
options: converging lens of focal length $12 \mathrm{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $20 \mathrm{ cm}$
converging lens of focal length $20 \mathrm{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $12 \mathrm{ cm}$
23368.sol:
The lens shown is a meniscus lens. We use the lens maker's formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right).

For the given lens, the first surface (left) is convex towards the object space, so its center of curvature $ C_1$ is to the right. By sign convention, $R_1 = +4 $\text{ cm}.

The second surface (right) is also convex towards the object space, so its center of curvature $ C_2$ is also to the right. By sign convention, $R_2 = +8 $\text{ cm}.

Given $\mu = 1.4$, we substitute these values into the formula:

\dfrac{1}{f} = (1.4 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{8} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.4 \times \left( \dfrac{2 - 1}{8} \right)

\dfrac{1}{f} =0.4 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{0.4}{8} = \dfrac{4}{80} = \dfrac{1}{20}

Therefore, $ f = +20 $\text{ cm}. Since the focal length is positive, the lens behaves as a converging lens.

Answer: converging lens of focal length 20 \mathrm{ cm}$

23767.subject: Physics
23767.text: A ball falls under gravity from a height of 10m with an initial downward velocity $u$. It loses three-fifths (or 60%) of its energy in collision and then rises back to 5m. The initial velocity $u$ is ($g = 10 \text{ ms}^{-2}$)
23767.sol:
Let the mass of the ball be $m$

Initial total energy of the ball at height $h_1 = 10$ is $E_i = mgh_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}mu^2$

$E_i = m(10)(10) + 0.5mu^2 = 100m + 0.5mu^2$

The ball loses $60\%$ of its energy upon collision, so the remaining energy is $0.4E_i$

The ball rises to a height $h_2 = 5$, so the final energy at the highest point is $E_f = mgh_2 = m(10)(5) = 50m$

Equating the remaining energy to the final energy gives $0.4(100m + 0.5mu^2) = 50m$

$40m + 0.2mu^2 = 50m$

$0.2u^2 = 10$

$u^2 = 50$

$u = \sqrt{50} \approx 7.07 ms^{-1}$

24584.text: If the bond length of $\mathrm{CO}$ bond in carbon monoxide is $1.128 \mathrm{~A}^{\circ}$, then what is the value of $\mathrm{CO}$ bond length in $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_5$ ?
24584.sol: The metal (Fe) makes the back bonding to $\mathrm{CO}$. The metal to ligand bonding creates a synergic effect which strengthens the bond $\mathrm{CO}$ and the metal ( $\mathrm{Fe}$ ). Which results in the contraction of $\mathrm{CO}$ bond length (Synergic means working together towards a common end. This is a bond formed by a ligand to metal ion which has a $\sigma$-bond from ligand to metal ion and the back donation of electron density from the metal to the $\pi^*$ orbitals on the ligand. Thus enhancing the acceptor strength of the p-orbital. Hence up to a point the effect of $\sigma$-bond formation strengthens the $\pi$-bonding or vice-versa. Due to this synergic effect bond order decreases.

25695.text: Let $X$ be the set of all five digit numbers formed using $1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 0$. For example, $22240$ is in $X$ while $02244$ and $44422$ are not in $X$. Suppose that each element of $X$ has an equal chance of being chosen. Let $p$ be the conditional probability that an element chosen at random is a multiple of $20$ given that it is a multiple of $5$. Then the value of $38p$ is equal to
25695.sol:
First we will find the sample space in which the number of five-digit numbers are divisible by $5$,

So, fixing zero at the last place we get,

$\mathop{- - - - 0}_{⏟}$

Now in first four place following number can take place,

$2224 \to \dfrac{4 !}{3 !} = 4\text{ways}$

$2244 \to \dfrac{4 !}{2 ! 2 !} = 6\text{ways}$

$2221 \to \dfrac{4 !}{3 !} = 4\text{ways}$

$2241 \to \dfrac{4 !}{2 !} = 12\text{ways}$

$2441 \to \dfrac{4 !}{2 !} = 12\text{ways}$

So, total sample space will be $4 + 6 + 4 + 12 + 12 = 38$

Now finding the number of favourable outcomes,

So, Number of five-digit numbers divisible by $5$ but 'not' by $20$

Now fixing $10$ in last two places, we get

$\mathop{- - - 1 0}_{⏟}$

So, the first three places can be occupied by,

$222 \to 1\text{ways}$

$224 \to 3\text{ways}$

$244 \to 3\text{ways}$

So, total number of numbers which are divisible by $5$ but not $20$ will be, $1 + 3 + 3 = 7$

So, favourable number of five-digit numbers that are divisible by $5$ and $20 = 38 - 7 = 31$

Hence, probability is given by, $p = \dfrac{31}{38}$

$⇒ 38p = 31$

25859.subject: Mathematics
25859.text: Consider a data consisting of $10$ observations $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}$, whose mean is $5$ and variance is $7$. If the mean and the variance of the first $8$ observations $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_8$ are $4$ and $3.5$, respectively, and $x_9 < x_{10}$, then the value of $3x_9 + 2x_{10}$ is ___________.
25859.sol:
Given $\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i}{10} = 5 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i = 50$

$\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2}{10} - 5^2 = 7 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 = 320$

For the first $8$ observations:

$\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i}{8} = 4 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 32$

$\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2}{8} - 4^2 = 3.5 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 8(3.5 + 16) = 156$

Subtracting the sums, we get:

$x_9 + x_{10} = 50 - 32 = 18$

$x_9^2 + x_{10}^2 = 320 - 156 = 164$

Using $(x_9 + x_{10})^2 = x_9^2 + x_{10}^2 + 2x_9 x_{10}$:

$18^2 = 164 + 2x_9 x_{10} \Rightarrow 2x_9 x_{10} = 324 - 164 = 160 \Rightarrow x_9 x_{10} = 80$

The numbers $x_9$ and $x_{10}$ are roots of the equation $t^2 - 18t + 80 = 0$.

$(t - 8)(t - 10) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 8, 10$

Since $x_9 < x_{10}$, we have $x_9 = 8$ and $x_{10} = 10$.

Therefore, $3x_9 + 2x_{10} = 3(8) + 2(10) = 24 + 20 = 44$.

Answer: $44$

25966.subject: Mathematics
25966.text:
Let $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{^}{k}$ be the unit vectors along the three positive coordinate axes. Let

$\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {b}_{3}\overset{^}{k}, {b}_{2}, {b}_{3} \in \mathbb{R}$

$\overset{\to}{c} = {c}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}, {c}_{1}, {c}_{2}, {c}_{3} \in \mathbb{R}$

be three vectors such that ${b}_{2}{b}_{3} > 0, \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$ and $\left(\begin{cases}0 & - {c}_{3} & {c}_{2} \\ {c}_{3} & 0 & - {c}_{1} \\ - {c}_{2} & {c}_{1} & 0\end{cases}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ {b}_{2} \\ {b}_{3}\end{array}\right) = \left(\begin{array}{ll}3 - {c}_{1} \\ 1 - {c}_{2} \\ - 1 - {c}_{3}\end{array}$\right) .$ Then, which of the following is/are TRUE?

$
25966.sol:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {b}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{c} = {c}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$

$\left[\begin{cases}0 & - {c}_{3} & {c}_{2} \\ {c}_{3} & 0 & - {c}_{1} \\ - {c}_{2} & {c}_{1} & 0\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ {b}_{2} \\ {b}_{3}\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3 - {c}_{1} \\ 1 - {c}_{2} \\ - 1 - {c}_{3}\end{array}\right]$

Now multiply and compare we get,

${b}_{2}{c}_{3} - {b}_{3}{c}_{2} = {c}_{1} - 3 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

${c}_{3} - {b}_{3}{c}_{1} = 1 - {c}_{2} . . . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

${c}_{2} - {b}_{2}{c}_{1} = 1 + {c}_{3} . . . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

Now applying operation $\text{equation}\left(1\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\right)\overset{^}{k}$ we get,

$\overset{^}{i}\left({b}_{2}{c}_{3} - {c}_{2}{b}_{3}\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left({c}_{3} - {b}_{3}{c}_{1}\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left({c}_{2} - {b}_{2}{c}_{1}\right) = {c}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k} - 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a} . . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$ $\left\{\text{given}\overset{\to}{a}\text{.}\overset{\to}{b}\text{=0}\right\}$

Again from (i)

$\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} - {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|cos\theta$, where $\theta = \overset{\to}{a} ∧\overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| \ge \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| ⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| \ge \sqrt{11}$

Given that $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0 ⇒ {b}_{2} - {b}_{3} + 3 = 0$

$⇒ {b}_{3} - {b}_{2} = 3$

Also ${b}_{2} - {b}_{3} > 0$

Now $\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 1 + {b}_{2}^{2} + {b}_{3}^{2}$

$= 1 + {\left({b}_{3} - {b}_{2}\right)}^{2} + 2{b}_{2}{b}_{3}$

$= 10 + 2{b}_{2}{b}_{3}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} > 10 ⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| > \sqrt{10}$

28009.subject: Chemistry
28009.text:
In a closed flask at $600$ K, one mole of X$_2$Y$_4$(g) attains equilibrium as given below :
$\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{XY}_2(g)$
At equilibrium, $75\%$ X$_2$Y$_4$(g) was dissociated and the total pressure is $1$ atm. The magnitude of $\Delta_r G^{\ominus}$ (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) at this temperature is __________. (Nearest Integer) (Given : R $= 8.3$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$; $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.3$, $\log 3 = 0.48$, $\log 5 = 0.69$, $\log 7 = 0.84$)
28009.sol:
The given equilibrium reaction is:
$\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{XY}_2(g)$

Initial moles: $1$
Degree of dissociation, $\alpha = 0.75$
Moles of $\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4$ at equilibrium $= 1 - \alpha = 1 - 0.75 = 0.25$
Moles of $\text{XY}_2$ at equilibrium $= 2\alpha = 2 \times 0.75 = 1.5$
Total moles at equilibrium $= 0.25 + 1.5 = 1.75$

Given total pressure, $P = 1$ atm.
Partial pressure of $\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4$, $P_{\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4} = \dfrac{0.25}{1.75} \times 1 = \dfrac{1}{7}$ atm
Partial pressure of $\text{XY}_2$, $P_{\text{XY}_2} = \dfrac{1.5}{1.75} \times 1 = \dfrac{6}{7}$ atm

The equilibrium constant $K_p$ is given by:
$K_p = \dfrac{(P_{\text{XY}_2})^2}{P_{\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4}} = \dfrac{(\dfrac{6}{7})^2}{\dfrac{1}{7}} = \dfrac{36}{7}$

The standard Gibbs free energy change is:
$\Delta_r G^{\ominus} = -RT \ln K_p = -2.3 RT \log K_p$

Calculating $\log K_p$:
$\log \left(\dfrac{36}{7}\right) = \log 36 - \log 7 = \log (2^2 \times 3^2) - \log 7$
$\log \left(\dfrac{36}{7}\right) = 2 \log 2 + 2 \log 3 - \log 7$
$\log \left(\dfrac{36}{7}\right) = 2(0.3) + 2(0.48) - 0.84 = 0.6 + 0.96 - 0.84 = 0.72$

Substituting the values into the $\Delta_r G^{\ominus}$ equation:
$\Delta_r G^{\ominus} = -2.3 \times 8.3 \times 600 \times 0.72$
$\Delta_r G^{\ominus} = -8246.88 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = -8.24688 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

The magnitude of $\Delta_r G^{\ominus}$ is $8.24688 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $8$.

Answer: $8$

(ii) Down the group electron affinity decreases due to size increases. EA order: $S > SeLi > Na$.

29103.subject: Chemistry
29103.text: The orange colour of ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}$ and purple colour of ${KMnO}_{4}$ is due to
options: $d \to d$ transition in ${KMnO}_{4}$ and charge transfer transitions in ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}$.
$d \to d$ transition in ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}$ and charge transfer transitions in ${KMnO}_{4}$.
29103.sol:
1. The deep blue colour of the solution ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}$ is because an electron from the Oxygen lone pair is transferred to low lying Chromate ion orbital.

  2. Oxidation number of Chromium in ${Cr}_{2}{{O}_{7}}^{2 -} ⇒ 2x + 7 \times \left(- 2\right)x = + 6$. The electronic configuration of Chromium is $1{s}^{2}2{s}^{2}2{p}^{6}3{s}^{2}3{p}^{6}4{s}^{1}3{d}^{5}$so it will lose six electrons to form ${Cr}^{+ 6}$.

  3. Electronic configuration of ${Cr}^{6 +} = 1{s}^{2}2{s}^{2}2{p}^{6}3{s}^{2}3{p}^{6}$since there are no electrons present in the d-orbital, the d-d transition will not occur.

  4. The oxygen atom in ${Cr}_{2}{{O}_{7}}^{2 -}$that act as a ligand and due to charge transfer transfers its one electron to chromium and due to which the coloured compound is formed.

  5. Similarly, in ${MnO}_{4}^{-}$the oxidation number of Manganese$⇒ x + 4 ( - 2 ) = - 1x = + 7$. The electronic configuration of Manganese is $1{s}^{2}2{s}^{2}2{p}^{6}3{s}^{2}3{p}^{6}4{s}^{2}3{d}^{5}$so it will lose seven electrons to form ${Mn}^{+ 7}$

  6. Electronic configuration of ${Mn}^{+ 7} = 1{s}^{2}2{s}^{2}2{p}^{6}3{s}^{2}3{p}^{6}$, here also no d-orbital is present so no d-d transition will take place.

  7. The oxygen atom in ${MnO}_{4}^{-}$ acts as a ligand and due to charge transfer transfers its one electron to manganese due to which a coloured compound is formed.

Therefore, ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}$ and ${KMnO}_{4}$ are coloured compounds due to charge transfer or ligand to metal transfer.

32535.subject: Chemistry
32535.text:
Consider the following data.
(i) $2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 3H_2(g) + 1200$ kJ/mol
(ii) $H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g) + 164$ kJ/mol
(iii) $HCl(g) + aq \rightarrow HCl(aq) + 83$ kJ/mol
(iv) $Al_2Cl_6(s) + aq \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 663$ kJ/mol
The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $Al_2Cl_6$ is :
32535.sol:
The given reactions with their enthalpy changes are:
(i) $2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 3H_2(g)$, $\Delta H_1 = -1200$ kJ/mol
(ii) $H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g)$, $\Delta H_2 = -164$ kJ/mol
(iii) $HCl(g) + aq \rightarrow HCl(aq)$, $\Delta H_3 = -83$ kJ/mol
(iv) $Al_2Cl_6(s) + aq \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq)$, $\Delta H_4 = -663$ kJ/mol

The required reaction for the enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $Al_2Cl_6$ is:
$2Al(s) + 3Cl_2(g) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(s)$

This target equation can be obtained by applying the following algebraic operations on the given equations:
Equation (i) $+ 3 \times$ Equation (ii) $+ 6 \times$ Equation (iii) $-$ Equation (iv)

Let us verify by adding the modified equations:
$2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 3H_2(g)$
$3H_2(g) + 3Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 6HCl(g)$
$6HCl(g) + aq \rightarrow 6HCl(aq)$
$Al_2Cl_6(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(s) + aq$

Summing the above reactions and canceling common terms on both sides, we get:
$2Al(s) + 3Cl_2(g) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(s)$

The enthalpy of formation is calculated as:
$\Delta H_f = \Delta H_1 + 3\Delta H_2 + 6\Delta H_3 - \Delta H_4$
$\Delta H_f = -1200 + 3(-164) + 6(-83) - (-663)$
$\Delta H_f = -1200 - 492 - 498 + 663$
$\Delta H_f = -2190 + 663 = -1527$ kJ/mol

Answer: $-1527$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

32791.subject: Mathematics
32791.sol:
Let $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$. Since $0 \leq x \leq \pi$, we have $0 \leq y \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

The given expression becomes $f(y) = 16\sin y \cos^3 y$.

Differentiating with respect to $y$:

$f'(y) = 16(\cos y \cdot \cos^3 y + \sin y \cdot 3\cos^2 y(-\sin y))$

$f'(y) = 16\cos^2 y(\cos^2 y - 3\sin^2 y)$

For maximum value, $f'(y) = 0$:

$\cos^2 y - 3\sin^2 y = 0 \Rightarrow \tan^2 y = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Since $y \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, $\tan y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Substituting $y = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ in $f(y)$:

$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 16\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\cos^3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 16 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^3$

$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 8 \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{8} = 3\sqrt{3}$

The maximum value is $3\sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $3\sqrt{3}$

32847.text: Let  $f\left(x\right) = \left|\begin{cases}1 + \sin^{2}x & \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ \sin^{2}x & 1 + \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ \sin^{2}x & \cos^{2}x & 1 + sin2x\end{cases}\right|, x \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$ . If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively are the maximum and the minimum values of $f$, then
32847.sol:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) = \left|\begin{cases}1 + \sin^{2}x & \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ \sin^{2}x & 1 + \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ \sin^{2}x & \cos^{2}x & 1 + sin2x\end{cases}\right|$

Applying ${C}_{1} \to {C}_{1} + {C}_{2} + {C}_{3}$

$f\left(x\right) = \left|\begin{cases}2 + sin2x & \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ 2 + sin2x & 1 + \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ 2 + sin2x & \cos^{2}x & 1 + sin2x\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left(2 + sin2x\right)\left|\begin{cases}1 & \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ 1 & 1 + \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ 1 & \cos^{2}x & 1 + sin2x\end{cases}\right|$

Applying ${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - {R}_{1}$

$f\left(x\right) = \left(2 + sin2x\right)\left|\begin{cases}1 & \cos^{2}x & sin2x \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left(2 + sin2x\right)\left(1\right) = 2 + sin2x$

Now, for

$x \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$

$⇒ 2x \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right]$

$⇒ sin2x \in \left[\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, 1\right]$

$⇒ 2 + sin2x \in \left[2 + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, 3\right]$

Hence,

$\beta = 2 + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\alpha = 3$

So,

${\beta}^{2} - 2\alpha = 4 + \dfrac{3}{4} + 2\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{19}{4}$

33163.subject: Mathematics
33163.text: Let a curve $y = y\left(x\right) pass through$ the $point \left(3, 3\right) and the area of the region under this curve, above the$x$-axis and between the abscissae $3 and x$\left(> 3\right)$ be ${\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3}$. If this curve also passes through the point $\left(\alpha, 6\sqrt{10}\right)$ in the first quadrant, then $\alpha$ is equal to _______.
33163.sol:
Given, the area of the region under this curve, above the $x$-axis and between the abscissae $3$ and $x\left(> 3\right)$ be ${\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3}$

So, ${∫}_{3}^{x}y d x = {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3}$

$⇒ {x}^{3}{∫}_{3}^{x}y d x = {y}^{3}$

Now differentiating both side w.r.t $x$, we get

$⇒ {x}^{3}y + 3{x}^{2}\dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = 3{y}^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ $\left\{\text{as given}{∫}_{3}^{x}y d x = {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3}\right\}$

$⇒ {x}^{4} + 3{y}^{2} = 3yx\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ 3xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3{y}^{2} + {x}^{4}$

Now put ${y}^{2} = t, y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} - \dfrac{2}{x}t = \dfrac{2}{3}{x}^{3}$

Now $IF = {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}$

So, solution is given by

$t \times IF = ∫ \dfrac{2}{3}{x}^{3} \times IF$

$⇒ \dfrac{t}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{3} + C$

Now given curve passes through $\left(3, 3\right)$ so $C = - 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{3} - 2$

So the equation of curve is $3{y}^{2} = {x}^{4} - 6{x}^{2}$

Now curve also passes through $\left(\alpha, 6\sqrt{10}\right)$

So, ${\alpha}^{4} - 6{\alpha}^{2} = 1080$

$⇒ \alpha = 6$

33340.text: The remainder, when ${7}^{103}$ is divided by $17,$ is
33340.sol:
Using the binomial expansion in ${7}^{103} = {\left({7}^{2}\right)}^{51} \cdot 7 = {\left(51 - 2\right)}^{51} \cdot 7$ we get,

${\left(51 - 2\right)}^{51} \cdot 7 = 7 \cdot \left(C0 51 {51}^{51} \cdot {2}^{0} - C1 51 {51}^{50} \cdot {2}^{1} + . . . . . . . - C51 51 {2}^{51}\right)$

Now $51$ is divisible by $17$, so when above equation is divided by $17$ we get, $7 \cdot \left(- {2}^{51}\right) as remainder,

Now again using binomial$ in 7 \cdot $\left(- {2}^{51}\right)$ = - 56{$\left({2}^{4}\right)$}^{12} = - 56{$\left(17 - 1\right)$}^{12}$ we get,

$- 56{$\left(17 - 1\right)$}^{12} = - 56$\left(C0 12 {17}^{12} \cdot {1}^{0} - C1 12 {17}^{11} \cdot {1}^{1} + . . . . . . . + C12 12 {1}^{12}\right)$

Now dividing above equation by $17$ we get,

$\left(- 56 \times 1\right)$ \div 17 = - 5$,

Now changing negative remainder to positive we get, $- 5 + 17 = 12$,

Hence, when ${7}^{103}$ divided by $17$ gives $12$ as remainder.

$

34044.text: Let $f: [ 0, \infty ) \to [ 0, \infty )$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\left[y\right]dy$ where $[ x ]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Which of the following is true?
options:
$f$ is continuous at every point in $[ 0, \infty )$ and
differentiable except at the integer points.
$f$ is both continuous and differentiable except at the integer points in $[ 0, \infty )$.
$f$ is continuous everywhere except at the integer points in $[ 0, \infty )$.
$f$ is differentiable at every point in $[ 0, \infty )$.
34044.sol:
$f: [ 0, \infty ) \to [ 0, \infty )$, $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\left[y\right]dy$

Let $x = n + f, f \in ( 0, 1 )$

$⇒ \left[x\right] = n, \left\{x\right\} = f$.

So

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left[y\right]dy + {∫}_{1}^{2}\left[y\right]dy + {∫}_{2}^{3}\left[y\right]dy + \ldots + {∫}_{n - 1}^{n}\left[y\right]dy + {∫}_{n}^{n + f}\left[y\right]dy$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{1}0dy + {∫}_{1}^{2}1dy + {∫}_{2}^{3}2dy + \ldots + {∫}_{n - 1}^{n}\left(n - 1\right)dy + {∫}_{n}^{n + f}ndy$

$f\left(x\right) = 0\left[1 - 0\right] + 1\left[2 - 1\right] + 2\left[3 - 2\right] + \ldots + \left(n - 1\right)\left[n - \left(n - 1\right)\right] + n\left[n + f - n\right]$

$f\left(x\right) = 0 + 1 + 2 + \ldots + \left(n - 1\right) + nf$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{n ( n - 1 )}{2} + nf$

$= \dfrac{[ x ] ( [ x ] - 1 )}{2} + \left[x\right]\left\{x\right\}$

Note $\lim_{x \to {n}^{+}}f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)}{2}$

$\lim_{x \to {n}^{-}}f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{( n - 1 ) ( n - 2 )}{2} + \left(n - 1\right)$

$= \dfrac{n ( n - 1 )}{2}$

35578.subject: Mathematics
35578.text:
Let $\alpha = 3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6}{11}\right)$ and $\beta = 3\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)$, where inverse trigonometric functions take only the principal values.
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\cos(\alpha+\beta) > 0$.
Statement II: $\cos(\alpha) < 0$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
35578.sol:
We are given $\alpha = 3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6}{11}\right)$ and $\beta = 3\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)$.

First, we find the range of $\alpha$.
Since $\dfrac{1}{2} < \dfrac{6}{11} < \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, we have $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) < \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6}{11}\right) < \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$.
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{6} < \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6}{11}\right) < \dfrac{\pi}{4}$
Multiplying by $3$, we get $\dfrac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.
Since $\alpha$ lies in the second quadrant, $\cos(\alpha) < 0$. Thus, Statement II is true.

Next, we find the range of $\beta$.
Since $0 < \dfrac{4}{9} < \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\cos^{-1}(x)$ is a decreasing function, we have $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) < \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right) < \cos^{-1}(0)$.
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{3} < \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right) < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
Multiplying by $3$, we get $\pi < \beta < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.
Thus, $\beta$ lies in the third quadrant.

Now, we determine the sign of $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$.
Adding the inequalities for $\alpha$ and $\beta$:
$\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \pi < \alpha + \beta < \dfrac{3\pi}{4} + \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{3\pi}{2} < \alpha + \beta < \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$
The angle $(\alpha + \beta)$ lies in the interval $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{9\pi}{4}\right)$, which covers the fourth quadrant and a part of the first quadrant. In both of these regions, the cosine function is strictly positive.
Therefore, $\cos(\alpha+\beta) > 0$. Thus, Statement I is true.

Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

Now,

But $n \in Z$, so $n = - 1, 0, 1$

So,

$\theta \in \left\{0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \pi\right\}$

So,

$\mathop{∑}_{\theta \in S}\sin^{2}\left(\theta + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 0 + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 2$

39135.text:
The charge accumulated on the capacitor connected in the following circuit is ______$\mu C$.

(Given $C = 150\muF )$
39135.sol:
Under the balanced condition, the capacitor will act as an open circuit.

The current $\left({i}_{1}\right)$ through the $1Ω$ resistor is given by

$\begin{cases}{i}_{1} & = & \dfrac{10V}{1Ω + 2Ω} \\ & = & \dfrac{10}{3}A\end{cases}$

The current $\left({i}_{2}\right)$ through the $6Ω$ resistor is given by

$\begin{cases}{i}_{2} & = & \dfrac{10V}{6Ω + 4Ω} \\ & = & 1A\end{cases}$

From the above diagram, it can be written that

${V}_{A} + {i}_{1} \times 1 - {i}_{2} \times 6 = {V}_{B} ⇒ {V}_{A} - {V}_{B} = 1 \times 6 - \dfrac{10}{3} \times 1 = \dfrac{8}{3}V$

Hence, the charge on the capacitor is given by

$\begin{cases}Q & = & C\left({V}_{A} - {V}_{B}\right) \\ & = & 150\mu F \times \dfrac{8}{3}V \\ & = & 400\mu C\end{cases}$

39358.text: A body of mass $2kg$ makes an elastic collision with a second body at rest and continues to move in the original direction but with one fourth of its original speed. What is the mass of the second body?
39358.sol:
From conservation of linear momentum
$mU = m\dfrac{U}{4} + MV$ . . . (i)
For elastic collision: $e = 1 = \dfrac{V - \dfrac{U}{4}}{u}$
$V = \dfrac{5U}{4}$ . . . (ii)
From equation (i) & (ii),
$mU = m\dfrac{U}{4} + M\left(\dfrac{5U}{4}\right)$
$m = \dfrac{m}{4} + \dfrac{5}{4}M ⇒ M = \dfrac{3m}{5} = 1.2kg$

Eliminating ${k}_{1}$ from (1) and (2) we get

$0 = \dfrac{1230}{500} - \dfrac{1230}{400} + ϕ$

$⇒ ϕ = 0 . 615eV$

42011.text: Water flows m a horizontal tube (see figure). The pressure of water changes by $700N{m}^{- 2}$ between $A$ and $B$ where the area of cross section are $40c{m}^{2}$ and $20c{m}^{2},$ respectively. Find the rate of flow of water through the tube. (density of water $= 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$ )
42011.sol:
Using equation of continuity
$40{V}_{A} = 20{V}_{B}$
$⇒ 2{V}_{A} = {V}_{B}$
Using Bernoulli’s equation
${P}_{A} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{A}^{2} = {P}_{B} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{B}^{2}$
$⇒ {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({V}_{B}^{2} - {V}_{A}^{2}\right)$
$⇒ \DeltaP = \dfrac{1}{2}1000\left({V}_{B}^{2} - \dfrac{{V}_{B}^{2}}{4}\right)$
$⇒ \DeltaP = 500 \times \dfrac{3{V}_{B}^{2}}{4}$
$⇒ {V}_{B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(\DeltaP\right) \times 4}{1500}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(700\right) \times 4}{1500}}\dfrac{m}{s}$
Volume flow rate $= 20 \times 100 \times {V}_{B} = 2732c{m}^{3} / s$

44258.subject: Physics
44258.text: ‘$n$’ polarizing sheets are arranged such that each makes an angle $45 °$ with the proceeding sheet. An unpolarized light of intensity $I$ is incident into this arrangement. The output intensity is found to be $\dfrac{I}{64}$ . The value of $n$ will be:
44258.sol:
When an unpolarized light passes through a polariser, the intensity of the emergent light from the polariser depends on the square of the cosine of the angle between the plane of the polariser and the direction of the incident light.

The formula to calculate the intensity $\left({I}_{1}\right)$ of the emergent light from a polariser which makes an angle $\theta$ with the direction of the incident light is given by

${I}_{1} = I\cos^{2}\theta . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where, $I$ is the intensity of the incident light.

Substitute $45 °$ for $\theta$ into equation (1) to obtain the intensity of the first emergent light.

$\begin{cases}{I}_{1} & = & I\cos^{2}45 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{I}{2}\end{cases}$

In a similar manner, the intensity $\left({I}_{2}\right)$ of the second emergent light can be written as

$\begin{cases}{I}_{2} & = & {I}_{1}\cos^{2}45 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{I}{4} \\ & = & \dfrac{I}{{2}^{2}}\end{cases}$

Thus, for $n$ number of such polarisers, the net intensity $\left({I}_{n}\right)$ of the emergent light can be written as

${I}_{n} = \dfrac{I}{{2}^{n}} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Comparing equation (1) with the given expression for the intensity, it can be concluded that

$n = 6$

Gonadotropins orgonadotropic hormones are those which stimulate the gonads (testes and ovaries),FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) stimulates growth ofovarian follicles and the secretion ofoestrogens in thefemale andspermatogenesis (formation of sperms) in themale . Luteinizing Hormone(LH) stimulatescorpus luteum of the ovary to secreteprogesterone in the females. In male, it activates theLeydig's (interstitial)cells of the testis to secreteandrogens. Somatotropins or somatotropic hormone orgrowth hormone stimulates growth directly and in conjugation with other hormones the target cells of these hormones are various body cells which undergo growth.Luteotropic hormones stimulates the corpus luteum of the ovary to secrete progesterone hormone. It is also called Prolactin Hormone (PRL) orMammotropin Hormone (MTH) because its main physiological effect is to activate growth of breast during pregnancy and secretion of mammary glands after child birth.Oxytocin (OT; pitocin) is secreted by posterior lobe of pituitary. It promotes contraction of the uterine muscles and myoepithelial cells of the lactating breast, ejecting the milk after child birth. Oxytocin is calledbirth hormone andmilk ejecting hormone.

52225.text:
Two balls of mass $M$ and $2M$ are thrown horizontally with the same initial velocity ${v}_{0}$ from top of a tall tower and experience a drag force of $- kv \left(k > 0\right)$ where $v is the instantaneous velocity.

Then,

$
options: the heavier ball will hit the ground further away than the lighter ball
the heavier ball will hit the ground closer than the lighter ball
both balls will hit the ground at the same point
both balls will hit the ground at the same time
52225.sol:
Only force resisting motion of particle in horizontal direction is drag force given by
$F = - kv$

But
$F = m \cdot {a}_{x}$

where, ${a}_{x} =$ acceleration in $x$-direction caused by drag force.
$∴m{a}_{x} = - kv ⇒ {a}_{x} = - \dfrac{kv}{m}$

$∴$ Acceleration of particle is $x$-direction is inversely proportional to mass.
So, decreases in velocity in $x$-direction for lighter particle will be more.
Hence, heavier mass will hit the ground further away from the lighter ball.

57167.text: Which of the following is trihydric phenol?

Phenols are classified by the number of hydroxyl groups bonded to the benzene ring: monohydric (one $\mathrm{-OH}$), dihydric (two $\mathrm{-OH}$), or trihydric (three $\mathrm{-OH}$).

Catechol (benzene-1,2-diol), resorcinol (benzene-1,3-diol), and quinol (benzene-1,4-diol) are all dihydric phenols.

Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol and contains three hydroxyl groups.

59153.text:
Which from following solutions exhibits minimum boiling point elevation under identical conditions?
(Assume complete dissociation)
59153.sol:
The boiling point elevation $\Delta T_b$ is given by $\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m$, where $i$ is the van't Hoff factor and $m$ is the molality. Since $K_b$ is constant for the solvent, $\Delta T_b$ is proportional to $i \cdot m$.

For $0.05\text{ m MgCl}_2$, which dissociates into three ions ($i = 3$), the product is $i \cdot m = 3 \times 0.05 = 0.15$.

Comparing with the other solutions: $0.2\text{ m KCl}$ gives $2 \times 0.2 = 0.4$, $0.1\text{ m NaCl}$ gives $2 \times 0.1 = 0.2$, and $1\text{ m AlCl}_3$ gives $4 \times 1 = 4.0$.

The minimum $i \cdot m$ value is $0.15$, corresponding to $0.05\text{ m MgCl}_2$.

The solution exhibiting the minimum boiling point elevation is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

59545.subject: Chemistry
59545.text: Which of the following statements is true about ideal gas ?
options: It shows deviation from Boyle's law and Charles' law.
Its molecules are not perfectly elastic.
Intermolecular attraction is present in it, hence a collision takes place with loss of kinetic energy.
59545.sol:
An ideal gas is a hypothetical concept and does not exist in reality. Real gases behave as ideal gases only under conditions of low pressure and high temperature.

According to the kinetic theory of gases, an ideal gas strictly obeys Boyle's law, Charles' law, and other gas laws under all conditions of temperature and pressure. The collisions between its molecules are perfectly elastic, and there are no intermolecular forces of attraction between its molecules.

Thus, the statement that it does not exist is true.

Answer: It does not exist.

60843.subject: Mathematics
60843.text: The locus of the points represented by $|z+3|-|z-3|=6$, where $z$ is a complex number, is....
60843.sol:
Let $z = x + iy$ with $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. The equation $|z+3| - |z-3| = 6$ describes a set of points where the difference of distances to $F_1 = -3$ and $F_2 = 3$ is constant. This defines a hyperbola, but with $2a = 6$ and $2c = |F_1 - F_2| = 6$, $a = c = 3$ implies the hyperbola degenerates.

The condition $|z - F_1| - |z - F_2| = |F_1 - F_2|$ requires that $z$ lies on the x-axis with $F_2$ between $F_1$ and $z$, so $y=0$. Substituting $z = x$, the equation becomes $|x+3| - |x-3| = 6$.

For $x \geq 3$, $|x+3| - |x-3| = (x+3) - (x-3) = 6$, which holds.
For $x < 3$, this equality fails: from $-3 \leq x < 3$, $x+3 - (3-x) = 2x$; setting $2x = 6$ gives $x=3$, a contradiction; for $x < -3$, $-(x+3) + (x-3) = -6 \neq 6$.

The locus is the ray $x \geq 3$ on the x-axis, corresponding to option D.

60909.text: If the function f is continuous at $x = \pi$, where $f(x) = \dfrac{1 - \cos[7(x - \pi)]}{5(x - \pi)^2}$, for $x \neq \pi$, then $f(\pi) = $
60909.sol:
Since the function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = \pi$, $f(\pi) = \lim_{x \rightarrow \pi} f(x)$.

Substituting $t = x - \pi$, as $x \rightarrow \pi$, $t \rightarrow 0$.

$f(\pi) = \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{1 - \cos(7t)}{5t^2}$

Using the identity $1 - \cos \theta = 2 \sin^2 \left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right):

$ f($\pi) = \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{2 \sin^2\left(\dfrac{7t}{2}\right)}{5t^2}

$ f($\pi) = \dfrac{2}{5} \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{7t}{2}\right)}{t} \right)^2$

$f(\pi) = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 \lim_{t → 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{7t}{2}\right)}{\dfrac{7t}{2}} \right)^2$

Since $\lim_{$\theta \rightarrow0} $\dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} =1$:

$f(\pi) = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{49}{4} \times1 = \dfrac{49}{10}$$

Answer: $$\dfrac{49}{10}$

61343.subject: Mathematics
61343.text: A particular solution of $3 \mathrm{e}^x \tan \mathrm{y} \mathrm{d} x+\left(1-\mathrm{e}^x\right) \sec ^2 \mathrm{y} \mathrm{dy}=0$ with $y(1)=\frac{\pi}{4} \quad$ is
61343.sol:
The differential equation is $3e^x \tan y\,dx + (1 - e^x)\sec^2 y\,dy = 0$.

Separating variables gives $\frac{3e^x}{1 - e^x}dx = -\frac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}dy$.

Integrating both sides: $\int \frac{3e^x}{1 - e^x}dx = -\int \frac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}dy$.

Using substitution $u = 1 - e^x$ on the left yields $-3\ln|1 - e^x|$.
With $v = \tan y$ on the right gives $-\ln|\tan y|$.

Equating and simplifying: $\ln|\tan y| = 3\ln|1 - e^x| + C$, leading to $\tan y = K(1 - e^x)^3$.

Applying $y(1) = \frac{\pi}{4}$ gives $1 = K(1 - e)^3$, so $K = \frac{1}{(1 - e)^3}$.

The particular solution is $\tan y = \left(\frac{1 - e^x}{1 - e}\right)^3$, matching option D.

Final answer: D

61569.text:
Bacteria increases at the rate proportional to the number of bacteria present. If the
original number N doubles in 4 hours, then the number of bacteria will be $4 \mathrm{ N}$ in
61569.sol:
Let $\mathrm{N}$ be the number of bacteria present at time $t_{0}$. Let $\mathrm{N}_{0}$ be the initial number of bacteria. Here $\frac{\mathrm{dN}}{\mathrm{dt}} \alpha \mathrm{N} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dN}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{KN} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dN}}{\mathrm{N}}=\mathrm{K} \mathrm{dt}$
$\therefore \int \frac{\mathrm{dN}}{\mathrm{N}}=\mathrm{K} \int \mathrm{dt} \Rightarrow \log \mathrm{N}=\mathrm{Kt}+\mathrm{C}$
When $\mathrm{t}=0, \mathrm{~N}=\mathrm{N}_{0}$
$$
\therefore \log N_{0}=C \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{N}{N_{0}}\right)=K t
$$
When $t=4, N=2 N_{0} \Rightarrow 4 K=\log 2$
$$
\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{4} \log 2 \\
\therefore \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{N}_{0}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{t}}{4} \log 2
\end{array}
$$
When $\mathrm{N}=4 \mathrm{~N}_{0}$, we get
$$
\log 4=\frac{t}{4} \log 2 \Rightarrow 2(\log 2)=\frac{t}{4}(\log 2) \Rightarrow t=8 \text{ hours }
$$
This problem can also be saved as follows :
Number of bacteria doubles in 4 hrs.
$\therefore$ If initial number of bacteria are $N$, then
After 4 hours number of bacteria become $2 \mathrm{~N}$.
After 8 hours, number of bacteria becomes $4 \mathrm{~N}$

63485.text: The number of 4-letter words formed from the English alphabet such that there are exactly 2 vowels and 2 consonants and no vowel is repeated, but consonants may be repeated is:
63485.sol:
The 4-letter word requires exactly 2 vowels and 2 consonants.

The number of ways to choose 2 positions out of 4 for the vowels is ^{4}C_{2}$.

Since no vowel is repeated, the number of ways to choose and arrange 2 distinct vowels from the 5 available vowels in the chosen positions is ^{5}P_{2}$.

The remaining 2 positions must be filled with consonants. Since there are 21 consonants and repetition is allowed, each position can be filled in 21 ways. The number of ways to fill the consonant positions is $21 \times 21 = (21)^2$.

The total number of 4-letter words formed is ^{4}C_{2} \times ^{5}P_{2} \times (21)^2$.

Answer: ${}^{4}C_2 \times {}^{5}P_2 \times (21)^2

64213.subject: Mathematics
64213.text: The acute angle between the line $4 x-2 y+13=0$ and the line which makes equal intercepts with the co-ordinate axes is
64213.sol:
To determine the acute angle between the lines, begin by finding their slopes. The first line, $4x - 2y + 13 = 0$, can be rearranged to slope-intercept form: $2y = 4x + 13$, yielding $y = 2x + \frac{13}{2}$, so $m_1 = 2$.

The second line makes equal intercepts on the axes. For intercept $a$, its equation is $x + y = a$, or in slope-intercept form, $y = -x + a$, so $m_2 = -1$.

The acute angle $\theta$ between lines with slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$ is given by $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2} \right|$. Substituting $m_1 = 2$ and $m_2 = -1$, compute $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{2 + 1}{1 - 2} \right| = \left| \frac{3}{-1} \right| = 3$.
Thus, $\theta = \tan^{-1}(3)$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

65556.sol:
Maximum current is drawn in a series LCR circuit at resonance.

At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance, so $\omega L = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$.

$C = \dfrac{1}{\omega^2 L} = \dfrac{1}{(2\pi f)^2 L}$

Given $L = 2\ \mu\text{H} = 2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{H}$ and $f = 10\ \text{kHz} = 10^4\ \text{Hz}$.

$C = \dfrac{1}{4\pi^2 f^2 L}$

Substituting the values and using $\pi^2 = 10$:

$C = \dfrac{1}{4 \times 10 \times (10^4)^2 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{40 \times 10^8 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{80 \times 10^2} = \dfrac{1}{8000}\ \text{F}$

Comparing with $C = \dfrac{1}{x}\ \text{F}$, we get $x = 8000$.

Answer: $8000$

66755.subject: Physics
66755.text: The equivalent inductance between A and B is equal to
66755.sol:
Let the given terminals be Node A and Node B.

Let us trace the connections and identify the nodes in the circuit. We can label the junction between the $1\text{ H}$, $2\text{ H}$, and $3\text{ H}$ inductors as Node C, and the junction between the $3\text{ H}$ and $4\text{ H}$ inductors as Node D.

The top wire connects Node A to the top end of the $2\text{ H}$ inductor and to Node D. Therefore, Node A, the top end of the $2\text{ H}$ inductor, and Node D are all at the same electrical potential. We can consider them all as Node A.

The bottom wire connects Node C to Node B. Therefore, Node C and Node B are at the same electrical potential. We can consider Node C as Node B.

Now, let us analyze the connection of each inductor:
1. The $1\text{ H}$ inductor is connected between Node A and Node C (which is Node B).
2. The $2\text{ H}$ inductor is connected between the top wire (Node A) and Node C (Node B).
3. The $3\text{ H}$ inductor is connected between Node C (Node B) and Node D (Node A).
4. The $4\text{ H}$ inductor is connected between Node D (Node A) and Node B.

From this analysis, it is clear that all four inductors are connected in parallel across the terminals A and B.

The equivalent inductance $L_{eq}$ of inductors in parallel is given by:
$\dfrac{1}{L_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{L_1} + \dfrac{1}{L_2} + \dfrac{1}{L_3} + \dfrac{1}{L_4}$

Substituting the given values:
$\dfrac{1}{L_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{1} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{4}$

Taking the least common multiple of the denominators, which is $12$:
$\dfrac{1}{L_{eq}} = \dfrac{12 + 6 + 4 + 3}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{L_{eq}} = \dfrac{25}{12}$

$L_{eq} = \dfrac{12}{25}\text{ H}$

Answer: $\dfrac{12}{25}$ H

66809.text: What is the phase difference between the flux linked with a coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field and the induced e.m.f. produced in it?
66809.sol:
The magnetic flux linked with a coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field is $\Phi = BA \cos(\omega t)$.

Faraday's law gives $\epsilon = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt}$. Differentiating $\Phi$, we obtain $\epsilon = BA\omega \sin(\omega t)$.

Using the identity $\sin(\omega t) = \cos(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2})$, the e.m.f. becomes $\epsilon = BA\omega \cos(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2})$.

The flux has phase $\omega t$ while the e.m.f. has phase $\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}$, so the e.m.f. lags the flux by $\frac{\pi}{2}$ radians.

The phase difference is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

67643.subject: Physics
67643.text: In the following figure, the magnitude of the magnetic field at point 'O' will be
67643.sol:
The magnetic field at point $O$ is the vector sum of the magnetic fields produced by the three segments of the current-carrying wire: the semi-infinite straight wire $AB$, the quarter-circular arc $BC$, and the semi-infinite straight wire $CD$.

For the semi-infinite straight wire $AB$, the perpendicular distance from $O$ is $r$. One end of the wire is at $B$ (subtending angle $0^\circ$) and the other extends to infinity (subtending angle $90^\circ$). The magnitude of the magnetic field at $O$ is:
$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (\sin 90^\circ + \sin 0^\circ) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$
By the right-hand rule, the direction of this field is out of the plane of the paper.

For the quarter-circular arc $BC$ of radius $r$, the angle subtended at the center $O$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at $O$ is:
$B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi} \dfrac{(\pi/2)}{r} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
The current flows from $B$ to $C$ in a counter-clockwise sense relative to $O$. By the right-hand rule, the direction of this field is also out of the plane of the paper.

For the semi-infinite straight wire $CD$, the perpendicular distance from $O$ is $r$. One end is at $C$ (subtending angle $0^\circ$) and the other extends to infinity (subtending angle $90^\circ$). The magnitude of the magnetic field at $O$ is:
$B_3 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (\sin 90^\circ + \sin 0^\circ) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$
By the right-hand rule, the direction of this field is out of the plane of the paper.

Since all three magnetic field components are in the same direction, the net magnetic field at $O$ is their sum:
$B_{net} = B_1 + B_2 + B_3$
$B_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$
$B_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} \left(1 + \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 1\right) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} \left(2 + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}\left(2+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

68665.text: For a particle executing S.H.M., its potential energy is 8 times its kinetic energy at a certain displacement '$x$' from the mean position. If '$A$' is the amplitude of S.H.M., the value of '$x$' is
68665.sol:
The potential energy of a particle executing S.H.M. at a displacement $x$ from the mean position is given by $U = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2x^2$

The kinetic energy of the particle at displacement $x$ is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$

Given that the potential energy is 8 times the kinetic energy:

$U = 8K$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2x^2 = 8 \times \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$

$x^2 = 8(A^2 - x^2)$

$x^2 = 8A^2 - 8x^2$

$9x^2 = 8A^2$

$x^2 = \dfrac{8}{9}A^2$

$x = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}A$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}A$

68723.text: A particle oscillates in straight line simple harmonically with period 8 second and amplitude $4 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m}$. Particle starts from mean position. The ratio of the distance travelled by it in $1^{\text{st }}$ second of its motion to that in $2^{\text{nd }}$ second is $\left(\sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}=1 / \sqrt{2}, \sin \frac{\pi}{2}=1\right)$
68723.sol:
Given: Period $T = 8$ s, amplitude $A = 4\sqrt{2}$ m, and the particle starts from the mean position.

Angular frequency is $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{\pi}{4}$ rad/s. The equation of motion is $x(t) = A \sin(\omega t) = 4\sqrt{2} \sin \$left($\frac{\pi}{4} t\right)$.

At $t = 1$ s, displacement is $x(1) = 4\sqrt{2} \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) =4$ m. Since motion is unidirectional from $x(0) = 0$, distance in the first second is $d_1 = 4$ m.

At $t = 2$ s, displacement is $x(2) = 4\sqrt{2} \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) =$==4\sqrt{2}$ m. Distance in the second second is $d_2 = |x(2) - x(1)| = 4(\sqrt{2} -1)$ m.

The ratio is \frac{d_1}{d_2} =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1},$ or 1 : $$(\sqrt{2} -1)$.

The correct choice is D.

69719.text: The energy spectrum of a black body exhibits a maximum around a wavelength '$\lambda$'. The temperature of the black body is now changed such that the energy is maximum around a wavelength $2\lambda/3$. The power radiated by the black body will now increase by a factor
69719.sol:
According to Wien's displacement law:

$\lambda_{m} T = b \Rightarrow T \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda_{m}}$

Given $\lambda_{1} = \lambda$ and $\lambda_{2} = \dfrac{2\lambda}{3}$.

$\dfrac{T_{2}}{T_{1}} = \dfrac{\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{2}} = \dfrac{\lambda}{\dfrac{2\lambda}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

According to Stefan-Boltzmann law, the power radiated by a black body is given by:

$P = \sigma A T^{4} \Rightarrow P \propto T^{4}$

The ratio of final power to initial power is:

$\dfrac{P_{2}}{P_{1}} = \left(\dfrac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}\right)^{4} = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{4} = \dfrac{81}{16}$

The power radiated increases by a factor of $\dfrac{81}{16}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{81}{16}$

70504.text:
A transverse displacement of vibrating string is $y=0.06 \sin \left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right) x \cos (120 \pi t)$.
If the mass per unit length of a string is $4 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ kg} / \mathrm{m}$, then the tension in the string will be
70504.sol:
Given the transverse displacement $y = 0.06 \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}x\right) \cos(120\pi t)$, comparison with the standard standing wave form $y = A \sin(kx) \cos(\omega t)$ identifies the wave number $k = \frac{2\pi}{3}$ rad/m and angular frequency $\omega = 120\pi$ rad/s.

The wave speed follows from $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{120\pi}{\frac{2\pi}{3}} = 180$ m/s.

For a string with mass per unit length $\mu = 4 \times 10^{-2}$ kg/m, the speed of transverse waves obeys $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}$. Solving for tension yields $T = v^2 \mu = (180)^2 (4 \times 10^{-2}) = 1296$ N.

The tension in the string is 1296 N.

70510.text: Two sources of sound are emitting progressive waves $y_1=4 \sin 710 \pi t$ and $y_2=3 \sin 702 \pi t$. The sources are placed close to each other. The number of beats heard per second and intensity ratio between waxing and waning are respectively

From the standard wave form $y = A \sin \omega t$, the amplitudes are $A_1 = 4$ and $A_2 = 3$, with angular frequencies $\omega_1 = 710 \pi$ rad/s and $\omega_2 = 702 \pi$ rad/s. The beat frequency is the difference in the individual frequencies. Since $f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}$, $f_1 = 355$ Hz and $f_2 = 351$ Hz, so $f_{\text{beat}} = |355 - 351| = 4$ beats/s. Under constructive and destructive interference, the maximum and minimum amplitudes are $A_{\text\max} = A_1 + A_2 = 7$ and $A_{\text\min} = |A_1 - A_2| = 1$. Since intensity $I \propto A^2$, the ratio is $\frac{I_{\text\max}{I_{\text\min}}} = \frac{7^2}{1^2} = \frac{49}{1}$. The number of beats per second is 4 and the intensity ratio is 49:1, so the correct option is C.

71184.subject: Biology
71184.text: Which layer of the blastocyst actively invades the endometrium?
71184.sol:
During the implantation of the blastocyst into the uterine wall, the outer layer of cells called the trophoblast differentiates into two distinct layers: an inner cytotrophoblast and an outer syncytiotrophoblast.

The syncytiotrophoblast is a multinucleated mass of cells without distinct cell boundaries. It secretes proteolytic enzymes that break down the extracellular matrix of the endometrial tissue, allowing it to actively invade the endometrium and establish a connection with the maternal blood vessels for nutrient exchange.

The inner cell mass develops into the embryo proper, while the zona pellucida degenerates prior to implantation to allow the blastocyst to attach to the uterine lining.

Answer: Syncytiotrophoblast

71363.subject: Biology
71363.text: Which type of sex determination is seen in honey bees?
71363.sol:
Honey bees exhibit a haplo-diploid mechanism of sex determination.

In this system, the sex of the offspring is determined by the number of sets of chromosomes it receives. Fertilized eggs develop into diploid females (queens or worker bees), which have 32 chromosomes. Unfertilized eggs develop into haploid males (drones) by parthenogenesis, which have 16 chromosomes.

Therefore, the sex determination in honey bees is of the haplo-diploid type.

Answer: Haplo-diploid type

71597.subject: Chemistry
71597.text: An organic compound 'A' on oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate forms an aldehyde having the molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$. What is compound 'A'?
71597.sol:
The aldehyde with the molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ is ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

Since the product is a two-carbon aldehyde (ethanal), the reactant 'A' must be a two-carbon primary alcohol.

Therefore, compound 'A' is ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$).

The reaction is: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC}} \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$

Answer: Ethanol

71624.subject: Chemistry
71624.text: Which of the following reagents converts acid chloride to aldehyde selectively?
71624.sol:
The conversion of an acid chloride to an aldehyde is known as the Rosenmund reduction.

The reagent used for this transformation is hydrogen gas in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulfate ($\text{H}_2$/Pd-$\text{BaSO}_4$).

Barium sulfate acts as a catalytic poison, which decreases the activity of palladium and prevents the further reduction of the newly formed aldehyde into a primary alcohol.

Strong reducing agents like $\text{LiAlH}_4$ and $\text{NaBH}_4$, as well as $\text{H}_2$/Pt, reduce acid chlorides completely to primary alcohols.

Answer: $\text{H}_2$/Pd-$\text{BaSO}_4$

72245.subject: Physics
72245.text: $C_p$ and $C_v$ are the specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume respectively. It is observed that $C_p - C_v = a$ for hydrogen gas and $C_p - C_v = b$ for carbon dioxide gas. The correct relationship between ' a' and 'b' is ( atomic weight of hydrogen , carbon and oxygen are 1u, 12 u and 16 u respectively)
72245.sol:
For a given gas, the molar heat capacities at constant pressure and constant volume are related by Mayer's relation:

$C_{P,m} - C_{V,m} = R$

The specific heat is defined as the heat capacity per unit mass. Therefore, the difference between the specific heats at constant pressure ($C_p$) and constant volume ($C_v$) is given by:

$C_p - C_v = \dfrac{R}{M}$

where $M$ is the molar mass of the gas.

For hydrogen gas ($H_2$), the molar mass is $M_{H_2} = 2 \times 1 = 2$ u. Thus:

$a = \dfrac{R}{2}$

For carbon dioxide gas ($CO_2$), the molar mass is $M_{CO_2} = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44$ u. Thus:

$b = \dfrac{R}{44}$

Taking the ratio of $a$ to $b$:

$\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{\dfrac{R}{2}}{\dfrac{R}{44}} = \dfrac{44}{2} = 22$

$\Rightarrow a = 22 b$

Answer: $a = 22\ b$

72289.text: Out of the following vectors, identify the one which is normal to the force, $\vec{F} = 4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$.
72289.sol:
Two vectors are normal to each other if their dot product is zero.

Given force vector $\vec{F} = 4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$.

Checking the dot product of $\vec{F}$ with each of the given vectors:

For option (1): $(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) \cdot (-6\hat{i}) = (4)(-6) + (-3)(0) = -24 eq 0$

For option (2): $(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) \cdot (7\hat{i}) = (4)(7) + (-3)(0) = 28 eq 0$

For option (3): $(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) \cdot (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) = (4)(3) + (-3)(4) = 12 - 12 = 0$

For option (4): $(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) \cdot (4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = (4)(4) + (-3)(3) = 16 - 9 = 7 eq 0$

Since the dot product is zero for the vector $3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$, it is normal to the given force vector.

72448.subject: Physics
72448.text: In Young's double slit, 18 fringes are observed to be formed in a certain segment of the screen when light of wavelength 400 nm is used. If the wavelength is changed to 600 nm, the number of fringes observed in the same segment of the screen is
72448.sol:
Let the length of the segment on the screen be $y$.

The fringe width is given by $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.

The number of fringes $n$ in the segment $y$ is $n = \dfrac{y}{\beta} = \dfrac{y d}{\lambda D}$.

This implies that $n \lambda = \text{constant}$, or $n_1 \lambda_1 = n_2 \lambda_2$.

Given $n_1 = 18$, $\lambda_1 = 400 \text{ nm}$, and $\lambda_2 = 600 \text{ nm}$.

Substituting the values, we get:

$18 \times 400 = n_2 \times 600$

$n_2 = \dfrac{18 \times 400}{600} = 12$

Thus, 12 fringes will be observed in the same segment.

Answer: $12$

75095.subject: General Ability
75095.text:
Consider the following statements in case of terrestrial planets:
I. Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are terrestrial planets having low densities as compared to other planets.
II. They lie between the Sun and the belt of asteroids.
III. Their lower gravity can hold the escaping gases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75095.sol:
Statement I is incorrect because terrestrial planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars) are primarily composed of rock and metal and have high densities compared to the Jovian planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune), which are gas giants with much lower densities.

Statement II is correct. The terrestrial planets are the inner planets, and their orbits lie between the Sun and the asteroid belt.

Statement III is correct. Because the terrestrial planets are smaller, they have lower gravity compared to the Jovian planets. This lower gravity is insufficient to hold escaping gases, which is why they do not possess thick, massive atmospheres of light gases like hydrogen and helium, unlike the giant outer planets.

Therefore, statements II and III are correct.

76905.subject: Mathematics
76905.text: If $A^2 + B^2 + C^2 = 0$, then what is the value of $\begin{vmatrix} 1 \text{ and } \cos C \text{ and } \cos B \\ \cos C \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } \cos A \\ \cos B \text{ and } \cos A \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix}$?
76905.sol:
Given $A^2 + B^2 + C^2 = 0$.

Since the square of any real number is non-negative, the sum of squares can be zero if and only if each number is zero.

Thus, $A = 0$, $B = 0$, and $C = 0$.

Substituting these values into the determinant, we get $\cos A = \cos 0 = 1$, $\cos B = \cos 0 = 1$, and $\cos C = \cos 0 = 1$.

The given determinant becomes:

$\begin{vmatrix} 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Since all rows are identical, the value of the determinant is 0$.

Answer: 0$

80318.sol:
Pteridophytes are the true land plants and show the following salient features:

80329.subject: Botany
80329.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect about gymnosperms?
options: Male and female gametophytes are free living
Most of them have narrow leaves with thick cuticle
80329.sol: The gametophyte generation is multicellular, haploid ($n$) very small in size, does not have conducting tissues and is dependent upon the sporophyte. The sporophytes of all gymnosperms are heterosporous since they produce two types of spores, namely the microspores and megaspores. The microspores are produced in structures, called microsporangia which are produced by modified fertile leaves called microsporophylls. The microsporophylls are compactly arranged in male cones or male strobili. In a microsporangium there are special diploid cells called microspores mother cells which undergo meiosis or reduction division to produce haploid microspores. Within the microspore, a reduced few celled male gametophyte generation develops. This entire structure is in the pollen grain which develops within the microsporangia. The megaspores are produced in megasporangia or ovules which are produced by modified fertile leaves called megasporophylls.

82852.subject: Physics
82852.text:
A box of mass $15$ kg is kept on the floor of a stationary trolley. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the trolley is $0.12$. Keeping the box in stationary state over the trolley, the maximum acceleration with which the trolley can be moved horizontally in m s$^{-2}$ is :
($g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
82852.sol:
Let the acceleration of the trolley be $a$.

In the frame of the trolley, a pseudo force $ma$ acts on the box in the direction opposite to the motion.

For the box to remain stationary relative to the trolley, the static friction force must balance this pseudo force.

The maximum static friction force available is given by $f_{s,\text{max}} = \mu_s N = \mu_s mg$.

Equating the pseudo force to the maximum static friction force gives the maximum acceleration:

$ma_{\text{max}} = \mu_s mg$

$a_{\text{max}} = \mu_s g$

Substituting the given values $\mu_s = 0.12$ and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$:

$a_{\text{max}} = 0.12 \times 10 = 1.2$ m/s$^2$

Answer: $1.2$

83942.subject: Zoology
83942.text: Which one of the following techniques does not serve the purpose of early diagnosis of a disease for its early treatment?
83942.sol:
Diagnosis of a disease at an early stage gives better opportunity to cure the same. Urine and serum analysis are a conventional way of diagnosis which can detect a disease only on the onset of the disease.

Recombinant DNA technology, Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) and Enzyme Linked Immuno-sorbent Assay (ELISA) are some of the techniques that serve the purpose of early diagnosis.

PCR is now routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients. ELISA is based on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction. A single stranded DNA or even an RNA, tagged with a probe is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells followed by detection using autoradiography. This is also used in detection of diseases.

Which of the following are the post-transcriptional events in an eukaryotic cell?

84824.sol:
The process of copying genetic information from one strand of the DNA into RNA is known as transcription. It occurs in the cytoplasm with the help of transcripting enzyme.

Transport of pre-mRNA to cytoplasm prior to splicing is a part of transcription.
The primary transcript is converted into functional mRNA after post transcriptional processing involves 3 steps as follows-
- Modification of 5' end by capping,
- Tailing,
- Splicing.

Base pairing of two complementary RNA is not on event of post-transcription. Hence, statements B, C, D are post-transcriptional modification events in eukaryotic cell.

85807.subject: Biology
85807.text:
The fundamental niche of a species is the full range of environmental conditions and resources a species can potentially occupy in the absence of limitations. The realized niche is the actual, smaller subset of the fundamental niche that the species occupies due to biotic limitations.

The distribution of populations of Species 1 and Species 2 over various levels towards the shore of an aquatic habitat is shown in the figure.

Consider the following statements based on the distribution.
(i) Competition for resources between Species 1 and Species 2 is mainly in the zones M and N.
(ii) Species 2 is a stronger competitor as compared to Species 1.
(iii) In absence of Species 2, Species 1 could prevail in zone O.
(iv) Species 2 probably has predators who thrive in zone O.
The correct statement(s) is(are):
85807.sol:
Based on the provided figure, we can determine the fundamental and realized niches for both species:
Species 1: Fundamental niche spans Zone M and Zone N. Realized niche is restricted to Zone M.
Species 2: Fundamental niche spans Zone N and Zone O. Realized niche is restricted to Zone N.

Let us evaluate the given statements:
(i) Competition occurs where the fundamental niches of the two species overlap. The overlap is exclusively in Zone N, not in Zone M. Therefore, statement (i) is incorrect.
(ii) In the overlapping Zone N, Species 2 is able to maintain its realized niche while Species 1 is excluded (its realized niche is only in Zone M). This indicates that Species 2 outcompetes Species 1 in this zone, making it a stronger competitor. Therefore, statement (ii) is correct.
(iii) The fundamental niche of Species 1 does not extend to Zone O. This means it cannot survive in Zone O due to abiotic limitations, regardless of the presence or absence of Species 2. Therefore, statement (iii) is incorrect.
(iv) The fundamental niche of Species 2 includes Zone O, but its realized niche does not. As stated in the question, the realized niche is smaller due to biotic limitations. Since Species 1 cannot exist in Zone O, the exclusion of Species 2 from Zone O must be due to another biotic factor, such as the presence of predators that thrive in that zone. Therefore, statement (iv) is a valid and probable inference.

Statements (ii) and (iv) are correct.

Answer: (ii) and (iv)
85807.meta: The fundamental niche of a species is the full range of environmental conditions and resources a species can potentially occupy in the absence of limitations.

Let, the roots be $\alpha, \beta, \alpha + 2 .
${S}_{1} = \alpha + \beta + \alpha + 2 = 2\alpha + \beta + 2 = 13 ⇒ 2\alpha + \beta = 11 ⇒ \beta = 11 - 2\alpha$

$⇒ 22\alpha + 22 - 4{\alpha}^{2} - 4\alpha + {\alpha}^{2} + 2\alpha = 15$
$⇒ 3{\alpha}^{2} - 20\alpha - 7 = 0 ⇒ \left(\alpha - 7\right)\left(3\alpha + 1\right)$ = 0$

92995.text: A long solenoid of cross-sectional radius $R$ has a thin insulated wire ring of uniform cross-section tightly put on its winding. The ring is made out of two different material such that one half of the ring has a resistance $10$ times that of the other half. The magnetic induction produced by the solenoid varies with time as $B = bt$, where $b$ is a constant. The magnitude of the electric field strength in the ring (other than the induced electric field) is
92995.sol:
Let us assume that the current in the ring is $i$ and the resistance of the two halves are $r$ and $10r$, then by faraday's law

$\left|\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right| = \pi{R}^{2}b = ir + i\left(10r\right)$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{\pi{R}^{2}b}{11r}$

The induced electric field in both the parts of the ring is

${E}_{ind} = \dfrac{R}{2}\dfrac{dB}{dt} = \dfrac{Rb}{2}$



Let $E$ be the field which is developed in each part due to charge accumulation at the junctions, then for the upper half

$\left({E}_{ind} + E\right)\piR = i\left(10r\right)$

and for the lower half

$\left({E}_{ind} - E\right)\piR = ir$

$⇒ 2E\piR - 9ir = 0$

$E = \dfrac{9ir}{2\piR}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{9r}{2\piR} \times \dfrac{\pi{R}^{2}b}{11r} = \dfrac{9}{22}Rb$

94538.text: A body cools in $7minutes$ from$60 ° C$ to $40 ° C$. What will be its temperature after the next $7minutes$? The temperature of the surrounding is $10 ° C$.
94538.sol:
According to Newton's law of cooling,

$- \dfrac{\text{d} \text{\theta}}{\text{dt}} = \text{K} \left(\text{\theta} - {\text{\theta}}_{0}\right)$

$\text{or} {∫}_{0}^{\text{t}} \text{dt} = \dfrac{1}{\text{K}} {∫}_{{\text{\theta}}_{1}}^{{\text{\theta}}_{2}} - \dfrac{\text{d} \text{\theta}}{\left(\text{\theta} - {\text{\theta}}_{0}\right)} \text{or} \text{t} = \dfrac{1}{\text{K}} {\text\log}_{\text{e}} \left[\dfrac{{\text{\theta}}_{1} - {\text{\theta}}_{0}}{{\text{\theta}}_{2} - {\text{\theta}}_{0}}\right]$

$\text{So here} 7 = \dfrac{1}{\text{K}} {\text\log}_{\text{e}} [ \dfrac{\text{60} - \text{10}}{\text{40} - \text{10}} ] \text{and also} 7 = \dfrac{1}{\text{K}} {\text\log}_{\text{e}} \left[\dfrac{\text{40} - \text{10}}{\text{\theta} - \text{10}}\right]$

$∴ \text\log [ \dfrac{\text{50}}{\text{30}} ] = \text\log \left[\dfrac{\text{30}}{\text{\theta} - \text{10}}\right] \text{or} \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{\text{30}}{\left(\text{\theta} - \text{10}\right)}$

i.e., $5\theta - 50 = 90$ or $\theta = 28 ° C$

94699.text: A diatomic ideal gas is used in a Carnot engine as the working substance. If during the adiabatic expansion part of the cycle, the volume of the gas increases from $V$ to $32V$. The efficiency of the engine is&
94699.sol:
The efficiency of cycle is

$η = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{2}}{{T}_{1}}$

For adiabatic process

$TV^{\gamma - 1} = constant$

For diatomic gas $\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}$

${T}_{1}{V}_{1}^{\gamma - 1} = {T}_{2}{V}_{2}^{\gamma - 1}$

${T}_{1} = {T}_{2}{\left(\dfrac{{V}_{2}}{{V}_{1}}\right)}^{\gamma - 1}$

${T}_{1} = {T}_{2}{\left(32\right)}^{\dfrac{7}{5} - 1} = {T}_{2}{\left({2}^{5}\right)}^{2 / 5} = {T}_{2} \times 4$

${T}_{1} = 4{T}_{2}$

$η = \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$

$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}k{\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}k\dfrac{x^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{3kx^{2}}{4m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{m}}\dfrac{x}{2}$

On collision with a block at rest

$∵$ Velocities are exchanged $⇒$ elastic collision between identical masses.

$∴ v = 3 = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{m}}\dfrac{x}{2}$

$⇒ 6 = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{m}}x$

$⇒ x = 6\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{3k}}$

$∴$ The initial energy of the spring is

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}k \times 36\dfrac{m}{3k} = 6m$

$U = 6 \times 0.1 = 0 .6 J$
